The High Society New Orleans Jazz Band

5:30 PM · Birdland Theater, Hell's Kitchen · $35.46 · ↻ Every Thursday

Led by veteran trumpeter Simon Wettenhall and Grammy winning pianist Conal Fowkes, The High Society New Orleans Jazz Band are a New Orleans style Jazz band which for decades have been Woody Allens band of choice for his movies, concert tours and weekly performances.The band have appeared on all the premiere concert stages of Europe and the United States. Band members have appeared in and provided music for Woody Allen movies including: Wild Man Blues, Sweet and Lowdown, Midnight in Paris, Blue Jasmine, Cafe Society, Magic In The Moonlight, and A Rainy Day In New York.Their driving sound is a testament to the ongoing relevance of New Orleans Jazz and they have an international fan base to prove it. Loved by critics and jazz aficionados alike, they have attracted Jazz icons like Chick Corea, Marian McPartland, Diana Krall and many others who sat in with the band during its twenty year residency at the Cafe Carlyle.Conal Fowkes (piano/vocals co-leader)Simon Wettenhall (trumpet/vocals co-leader)Tom Abbott (clarinet)Harvey Tibbs (trombone)Josh Dunn (banjo)Brian Nalepka (bass/vocals)Kevin Dorn (drums)

A Ghost in Your Ear

7:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Every Thursday

When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

Susto (solo) with special guest Daniel Ray Hillsinger

7:00 PM · Drom, East Village · $32.92

SUSTO (Solo) - Justin Osborne is a singer, songwriter, and storyteller best known as the founder and frontmanof SUSTO. Since founding the band in 2013 while living in Havana, Cuba, Osborne has built anexpansive catalog rooted in deeply personal lyricism and a sound that moves between SouthernGothic, folk, rock, country, and psychedelia.Across SUSTO, the roots-oriented Susto Stringband, and his solo performances, Osborne'ssongwriting remains the throughline---confessional, searching, and shaped by love, loss,change, resilience, and the strange beauty of everyday life. Performing solo brings those songsback to their foundation, putting Osborne's voice, lyrics, and storytelling front and center andoffering an intimate look at the songwriter behind the catalog. Daniel Ray Hillsinger Website - https://danielrayhilsinger.com/ Spotify - https://open.spotify.com/artist/0ZugMhJumMgfKPfAXFzLNU IG - https://www.instagram.com/danielrayhilsinger/

Ron Carter's Great Big Band

7:00 PM · Birdland Jazz Club, Hell's Kitchen · $45.76

Ron Carter is among the most original, prolific and influential bassists in jazz with more than 2,000 albums to his credit. Beginning his career in the 1960s with Jaki Byard and Eric Dolphy, Cannonball Adderley, and a five year stint with the Miles Davis Quintet, Ron also performed and recorded with notables including Bill Evans, B.B. King, and Dexter Gordon. Ron Carters various ensembles, big band to trio, feature a whos who of the finest players on the NYC scene with, an absolute commitment to musical sublimity [that] exudes refined elegance and sonic power. Raffaella

8:15 PM · Lucinda's, East Village · $27.11

Over the past six years NYC native Raffaella has been living in Minneapolis and writing her debut album - a midwestern-soaked meditation on faith, belonging, and the beauty of believing without proof. On October 22nd, she's coming home to share it with us. Not only will she give us a sneak peak performance of the whole record, but she will also hand out a free CD to every ticket holder: , "rdquo" -> Live music should be rewarded with analogue party favors - I want this to be an experience you can have and then literally hold." As one of pop's sharpest observers of human behavior, Raffaella pulls meaning out of weakness like a magnet and turns big existential questions into something warm and lived-in. The record's first single, Courtney, is out now. Previous tours include opening for Samia, Liz Phair, Del Water Gap and more.
